To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of urea to diets containing wet corn glucose feed (WCGFs) improved the performance of finishing cattle.
corn processing did not influence feed intake, growth performance, or carcass characteristics when fed with wet corn gluten feed and urea.
the addition of urea to diets containing wet corn processing and high-moistur corn had no effect on feedlot performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of processing corn and the inclusion of urea in diets containing wet corn-gluten feed on cattle performance.
the development of new technologies and the use of existing technologies in a new way to increase the value of wet corn gluten feed and improve the efficiency of cattle production.
the effect of the type of processing of corn on the performance of finishing cattle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
corn processing method and protein level in finishing diets containing WCGF had no effect on feedlot performance.

the effects of corn grain processing method and protein concentration in finishing diets containing wet corn-gluten feed on feedlot performance and carcass characteristics are not consistent and depend on the specific corn processing method and protein level.
processing corn with steam-flaking, rolling, and grinding, and adding urea to diets containing wet corn gluton feed, did not affect performance or carcass characteristics of steers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of WCGF can be an economical way to reduce the cost of feed and improve the efficiency of gain of cattle fed in the feedlot.
processing method of corn in finishing diets containing wet corn-gluten feed did not affect feedlot performance or quality of carcasses.
processing method and protein concentration in finishing diets containing WCGF had little impact on performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the processing of corn has an impact on the performance of cattle fed corn-based diets containing WCGF.
we can reduce the cost of finishing diets containing corn gluten feed by replacing some of the corn in the diet with corn gluten feed.
the use of wet corn gluten feed can reduce feed costs by up to 30% while still maintaining the performance of feedlot cattle.
